messages:
margo: Quick q — we merged a tiny log-format fix into runtime main. Only touches debug logging output, no behavioral change. Do we bump patch or skip?

sam: lean toward skip if there's truly no functional change. Docs-only or buildmeta-only usually skip.

kai: it's runtime code, not docs. If anyone pins exact semver (major.minor.patch) they won't get the fix unless we bump. I'd patch.

nate: +1 patch. Also, our deploybot uses patch bumps to trigger release notes and stable-channel promotion, so skipping might hide the change.

olga: small caveat: semver allows build metadata (e.g. 1.2.3+buildmeta) but many package managers ignore it for version resolution. Customers pin to exact patch a lot.

eve: deploy-bot: Canary deployment available. Will queue canary if you request a release. Use `/deploy canary` to start.

margo: noted. I worry about churn — this is very low risk. If we do a patch bump should we mark it as "no user impact" in release notes?

sam: yes, short release note: "debug log formatting only — no runtime behavior change." That keeps changelog honest.

kai: operational question: should we also add a stable-channel pin until we verify no regressions? We can unpin after 1-2 hours.

nate: I'd prefer a short pin window (30m) on stable. If canary looks good, auto promote. That minimizes blast radius.

release-bot: Release bot: If you request a patch bump I will: 1) create a release candidate branch, 2) add release note template, 3) schedule canary -> stable promotion per defaults. Reply `@release-bot bump patch` to proceed.

olga: One more note for decision log: we should be explicit about policy exceptions. Nonfunctional runtime formatting changes are borderline; prefer patch when code touched vs docs-only. Saves support churn.

margo: OK consensus forming. Plan: bump patch, tiny release note, canary then 30m stable pin, unpin if no errors. I'll open the PR and ping release-bot.

eve: deploy-bot: Canary queued (`deploy/canary runtime@patch`). ETA ~5m.

sam: Throw a short smoke test: `curl -sS $CANARY_URL/health && grep -q "ok" /tmp/canary.log` — validate logs emit new debug header.

margo: will run those and post results. If all green, @release-bot bump patch and promote.

margo: (10m later) canary looks clean, logs show new header, no errors in traces.

release-bot: Release bot: Acknowledged. `@release-bot bump patch` received. Creating v2.7.5, adding release note: "runtime: debug log formatting — no functional change." Scheduling canary->stable per policy.

nate: 👍 I'll monitor the stable rollout and watch latency/error dashboards for 1 hour.

margo: thanks everyone. Follow-up: add a short FR to release docs specifying: "runtime formatting-only changes -> prefer patch bump when code changed; docs-only -> skip." I'll file that.

olga: thanks. This keeps pinning semantics clear for customers who lock patches.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Stable promotion complete. v2.7.5 is in stable channel. Pin window (30m) expired with no anomalies.

margo: closing thread — will add docs FR and link the PR in case someone needs the history. :tada:
